newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end strong as futures lead way up.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end strong as futures lead way up.

text.p: Robust gains in heavyweight industrial stocks, fomented by futures-basket trading, led South African shares up to the close as the market ignored the impact of a nationwide strike by the country's biggest union.
Dealers said stock gains were also in response to a hefty slide in industrials on Friday on expectations of a weak Wall Street, which went on to end flat.
The industrial index finished up 50.2 points to 8,290.4 as the industrial near-month futures contract held at 7,950/54 from 7,910 in late trade.

Overall turnover was subdued at around 371 million rand's worth as some players hung on the sidelines as members of the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) protested against new employment legislation.
Gold shares had another lacklustre day as bullion dipped below $344, pushing the index to yet another fresh four year closing low at 1,166.6 -- a fall of 7.6 points.
The overall index ended up 39.6 points at 7,061.3.
